transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-08-31 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Eliot Chen (Redwood AE); Maya Patel (Redwood SE); Samir Rao (Redwood CSM); Jordan Kline (NimbleLens, Head of ML Ops); Priya Shah (NimbleLens, CTO); Rafael Morales (NimbleLens, Platform)

Summary: Quick renewal check-in focused on contract extension options, adding eu-west region and an on-prem proof for sensitive workloads, plus runbook for latency failover and burst capacity. Action items and next steps agreed at end.

Topics: Renewal terms, Dedicated vs Hosted for EU data, On-prem pilot timeline, Latency SLOs, KMS and audit logs, Autoscaling/burst profiles, Benchmarks to validate tail latency.

-- TRANSCRIPT --
[00:00:00] Eliot (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking time. quick intro round, then we'll jump into the renewal and region plan.
[00:00:12] Jordan (NimbleLens): Hey, Jordan here, thanks. will try to keep it tight, we've got a product sync right after.
[00:00:19] Maya (SE): Hi all, Maya from Redwood infra. I'll speak to the autoscale and performance pieces.
[00:00:25] Priya (CTO): Priya here. main ask — can we get eu‑west activation and also a path for an on‑prem pilot for PHI workloads.
[00:00:35] Samir (CSM): Samir, I'll follow up on billing/pricing items and SOW updates.
[00:00:42] Rafael (Platform): Rafael, platform engineer. I'll be hands on for the benchmarks.

[00:01:10] Eliot (AE): Great. quick status: your contract ends mid‑October, current commit covers US regions only, with the existing throughput block. you sign a 12‑month extension, we can add an eu cluster and a scoped private pilot for on‑prem. pricing varies depending on Dedicated vs Hosted + private plane. Jordan, is that aligning with what you expect?
[00:01:30] Jordan: yeah that's the ask. second item — last month we saw some tail latency spikes under heavy inference for longer prompts. can we get a guarantee or at least a mitigation path?
[00:01:44] Maya: totally. spikes usually root from KV cache misses and model variant fallbacks, also batch windows. we can tune batching and pre‑warm pads, also suggest prefix caching for common prompts.
[00:02:02] Priya: when you say prefix caching — is that something in the hosted product or only on Dedicated?
[00:02:08] Maya: both. Hosted has managed prefix/K V cache, um excuse me — managed KV cache, Dedicated gives you more control for sticky caches and warm nodes. clarity: for on‑prem the caching layer will be part of the runtime we ship, but requires local disk or shared mem config.

[00:03:00] Rafael: one constraint — our infra team wants to avoid persistent disk encryption key management complexity; we prefer K M S integration with our cloud provider. can Redwood do BYOK?
[00:03:12] Samir: yes, we support KMS BYOK for Dedicated and Private — HSM integrations are available with the enterprise add‑on. I'll attach the security pack.

[00:04:30] Eliot: let's talk numbers — current commit is 400M tokens / month. you're forecasting a 2.5x increase with EU traffic. two options: 1) uplift commit and add eu region as hosted with reserved capacity, cheaper but slightly longer lead time; 2) Dedicated pool in eu with reserved GPUs — better control and SLOs but higher base cost.
[00:05:00] Priya: what's the delta on latency for Hosted eu vs Dedicated eu? ballpark.
[00:05:06] Maya: hosted eu with our multi‑tenant nodes is typically 30–60ms p50 on common model families, p95 can be in the 200–400ms range depending on sequence length. Dedicated with pinned nodes and local KV warms sees p95 drop to 120–180ms in our benchmarks. ymmv.
[00:05:28] Jordan: and for long sequences — say 2k tokens — what's the tail?
[00:05:33] Maya: longer sequences amplify compute; p95 could go up to 600–800ms hosted, Dedicated with tensor kernels optimized and quantized weights we've observed p95 in the 300–450ms band. again depends on model.

[00:06:15] Rafael: hmm, we have real‑time inference for some features where >500ms is problematic. our idea was to keep those endpoints on Dedicated and non‑real time on hosted. does Redwood let us route per route?
[00:06:26] Maya: yes, per‑route routing policies — you can pin specific endpoints to the Dedicated pool and fallback to hosted for capacity shortages. built‑in fallback is available.

[00:07:10] Priya: cost tradeoffs: if we go Dedicated for production EU real‑time endpoints and Hosted for lower‑priority workloads, what's typical cost uplift?
[00:07:20] Eliot: rough order: Dedicated baseline is ~1.6–2x hosted at steady state for the same throughput because of reserved GPUs and isolation. but effective cost per generated token can be lower if you get higher utilization; also autoscale and burst policies reduce incremental spend. we'll send a small model‑specific TCO doc.

[00:08:05] Jordan: about uptime and failover — if eu region has an incident, can traffic fail over to us‑west? what's the egress and latency cost?
[00:08:16] Maya: yes, smart routing can failover to us‑west. you can set a latency threshold or error rate policy. egress depends on your cloud provider and data residency; we can preserve response caching to reduce cross‑region hits. note: some customers prefer read‑only fallbacks to avoid data residency violations.

[00:09:40] Rafael: security review — we'll need SOC2 docs, ISO attestation, SSO via SAML, and API audit logs retained for 12 months. do we have that on file?
[00:09:52] Samir: we do. I'll share our compliance pack and point to the audit log retention options — retention is configurable under enterprise.

[00:11:05] Priya: on‑prem pilot — timeline wise we want a small air‑gapped PoC to validate PHI flow before we do a full migration; can Redwood point of contact the infra team?
[00:11:15] Eliot: yes, SE + infra will run the onboarding. typical PoC is 6–8 weeks: week 1 prep and network, weeks 2–4 deploy and tune, weeks 5–6 performance runs and sign off. some customers compress this.
[00:11:34] Jordan: ok that works. we also need to validate KV cache behaviour on‑prem.
[00:11:39] Maya: on‑prem uses the same runtime and KV semantics; main differences are network fabric and disk latencies — we'll give recommended JVM/tweaks and mem configs.

[00:12:45] Eliot: let's capture concrete asks: NimbleLens wants a) eu‑west activation, b) Dedicated subset for real‑time endpoints, c) on‑prem PHI pilot scoped, and d) renewal for 12 months with uplift. Samir will update the SOW.

[00:13:10] Jordan: quick note — our procurement is sensitive to minimum revenue commitment; if we add EU capacity we prefer a 9‑month ramp payment schedule vs annual frontload. any flexibility?
[00:13:23] Eliot: yes, we can propose staged billing in the SOW — monthly ramp payments for the first 90 days, then normal cadence. I'll include options.

[00:14:05] Rafael: for the benchmark — we want to run a 48‑hour litmus against eu nodes with a mixed prompt distribution. can Redwood provide a lane or seeded traffic to validate?
[00:14:16] Maya: we can provide a dedicated test pool and a script; also we'll share the sample prompt set and guidance on measuring tail latency.

[00:15:30] Priya: curious — we evaluated Anthropic for a subset of LLM workloads, they offered lower per‑token in the hosted plan but have less mature on‑prem story. any notes on migration/blend?
[00:15:42] Eliot: we've seen customers mix providers — Redwood supports multi‑model routing. the main friction is model semantics and eval regressions; Redwood Optimize can run prompt set diffs to guard quality.

[00:17:00] Samir: okay i'll note items to attach: SOC2 pack, KMS BYOK doc, amended SOW template, per‑route TCO spreadsheet.

[00:18:20] Maya: technical aside — for the long sequences you mentioned, quantized model variants reduce memory and can cut p95 significantly but might have slight quality delta, we'll run evals.
[00:18:36] Jordan: acceptable as long as we gate it behind evals.

[00:20:00] Rafael: networking — for the on‑prem pilot, we want minimal open egress; can Redwood run without outbound to Redwood control plane? basically air‑gapped.
[00:20:12] Maya: we support a private control plane option where the control plane is customer‑hosted — totally possible but adds ops complexity; we'll propose a thin management proxy and offline installer.

[00:22:00] Priya: timeline check: if we sign amendment by mid‑Sept can we have eu activation by end‑Oct?
[00:22:09] Eliot: tight but doable if we prioritize — hosted EU can be turned on in 3–4 weeks after billing and contract; Dedicated provisioning can take 6–8 weeks for GPU pools.

[00:24:30] Jordan: cost ask — show me 3 scenarios in the new quote: minimal uplift hosted eu, dedicated eu for real‑time only, and dedicated + on‑prem pilot bundled.
[00:24:41] Eliot: will do.

[00:26:00] Rafael: small detail — what telemetry do you expose for per‑token cost? we need token‑level tagging and tracebacks into our logs.
[00:26:10] Maya: you can push token metadata in headers, and our SDK will emit token counts per request; console has token breakdown per route and per model.

[00:28:00] Priya: one more security question — do we support SAML SCIM for automated provisioning?
[00:28:07] Samir: yes SAML + SCIM available for enterprise accounts; we'll share the SAML config doc.

[00:30:12] Jordan: let's recap what we need from you: 1) amended SOW with ramp billing options, 2) three pricing scenarios, 3) security/compliance pack, 4) test pool and benchmark scripts, 5) timeline for Dedicated vs Hosted.
[00:30:27] Eliot: correct — and we'll add a recommended autoscale and caching profile for your traffic.

[00:32:00] Maya: action on my end — I'll prepare the autoscaling + burst estimate and a recommended prefix caching config, plus suggested quantization profiles for your model family.

[00:34:15] Rafael: question on SLA penalties — for Dedicated what are availability SLAs and credits?
[00:34:22] Eliot: Dedicated SLA is 99.9% monthly uptime with credits per the enterprise agreement; I'll include exact clauses.

[00:36:40] Priya: about the on‑prem PoC acceptance criteria — we want 1) parity on p95 vs hosted baseline (within 20%), 2) KV cache correctness, 3) audit log completeness. can we formalize that?
[00:36:53] Maya: yes we can draft a short acceptance checklist.

[00:38:10] Jordan: any known gotchas for EU data residency when failing over to US? need to flag legal.
[00:38:18] Samir: legal needs to confirm but we recommend read‑only fallback and explicit consent on cross‑region failovers to avoid residency violations. I'll loop legal if you want.

[00:40:00] Rafael: ok I'll prepare traffic breakdown by route and time of day — that should help autoscale tuning. expect that by next Friday.

[00:41:30] Eliot: next steps recap: we'll share SOW + three pricing scenarios by 2026‑09‑03; Maya will share technical docs and benchmark script by 2026‑09‑02; Samir to share compliance pack today; NimbleLens to run the 48h litmus and return logs by 2026‑09‑10.
[00:42:05] Priya: good. also please add the staged billing option in the SOW.

[00:43:20] Jordan: any final questions from Redwood?
[00:43:24] Maya: none from me.
[00:43:27] Samir: i'll reach out to legal contacts for residency questions.

[00:44:00] Eliot: thanks everyone — we'll circulate notes and action items.
[00:44:06] Priya: thanks.
[00:44:09] Rafael: thanks all.

-- END OF TRANSCRIPT --

Recap (auto): Agreement to propose a 12‑month renewal with an EU activation. NimbleLens prefers Dedicated for latency‑sensitive endpoints and an on‑prem PHI pilot. Redwood to deliver SOW, pricing scenarios, benchmark kit, and security docs. Explicit next steps and dates captured above.

Attachments referenced: security_compliance_pack.pdf (shared by Samir after call), nimblelens_benchmark_script.tar.gz (Maya), draft_sow_v2.docx (Eliot), per_route_tco.xlsx (Eliot).

Notes on transcript quality: speaker overlaps and a few acronyms mistranscribed (KV cache as 'K V cash' in earlier auto notes).
